criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines (test modules excluded). Every new child file under crates/athena-core/src/reading/ is also under 1500 lines, and no function exceeds 200 lines. Check by reading the files.
criteria.evidence: In the candidate reading.rs, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` starts at line 1362, so production code is at most 1361 lines (found with the Grep tool). The diff stat gives the child files' total sizes: checks 657, outcome 352, replay 410, retry 839, surveys 996, terms 300 and topics 560, all under 1500. Functions were moved without edits, and the base's longest function, build_reading, was 147 lines, so none exceeds 200.

criteria.criterion: Every previously public item of crate::reading (for example check_defined_terms, check_outcome_state, plan_entry, earlier_attempt, retry_findings, same_scope) is still reachable at the same path. The diff shows `pub use` re-exports and no edits to callers outside reading.rs, apart from mod declarations.
criteria.evidence: reading.rs lines 57-71 declare `mod checks; ... mod topics;` and `pub use checks::*; ... pub use topics::*;`. The diff stat shows that no caller (run/, steward.rs, plan.rs, status.rs, hestia.rs, athena-cli) changed, and the whole workspace builds. The one file edited outside reading/ is tests/refusal_corpus.rs. It does not use the API: it reads the source text with include_str!, so it had to learn the new file locations.

criteria.criterion: The diff is a pure move. Function bodies, constants and tests are unchanged apart from visibility (pub(super) or pub(crate)) and import paths. No logic edits.
criteria.evidence: Lines in each child file that do not line up with the base reading.rs (histogram diff): checks 14, outcome 22, replay 7, retry 16, surveys 47, terms 17, topics 11. In the parent, 49 lines were added and 4100 removed; the 49 include the 15 mod and pub use lines. A Grep for `pub(super)`/`pub(crate)`/`use `/`//!` lines in the child files gives near-identical counts: 14, 22, 7, 18, 40, 16 and 12. The surveys difference matches lines that rustfmt re-wrapped after the longer `pub(super) const ... =` prefix. The -G pickaxe shows no `#[test]` line added or removed, and all 172 reading tests are present. In tests/refusal_corpus.rs, the READING_SOURCE const became a reading_source() function that joins the child files and the parent; every assertion is unchanged. Limit: Athena policy denied a Grep over the saved full moved-lines diff, so I did not see every line that fails to line up.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`, including tests/refusal_corpus.rs and the reading tests. All pass, with the same tests and no removed or ignored ones.
criteria.evidence: refusal_corpus: 20 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. reading:: unit tests: 172 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, matching the 172 `#[test]` attributes in reading.rs, and the diff touches no `#[test]` lines. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed in CI run 42461965381.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, and `cargo build` succeeds for the whole workspace.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded clippy (-D warnings) and fmt --check both passed in CI run 42461965381 for commit 4af71c8. I ran `cargo build --workspace`, which finished with every crate, including athena-cli and xtask, compiling.

criteria.criterion: athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are not changed. The change is one focused structural split.
criteria.evidence: Changed files: CHANGELOG.md, reading.rs, the seven reading/*.rs files and tests/refusal_corpus.rs. athena.toml, defaults.toml and .github/workflows are untouched. The CHANGELOG entry sits under [Unreleased] > Changed.

findings.summary: Three changed files are outside the expected-deliverables list: reading/replay.rs, reading/surveys.rs and tests/refusal_corpus.rs.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list names retry, checks, terms, outcome, topics and CHANGELOG only. The two extra child modules fit the reading's own description, which says to move cohesive groups into child modules. The refusal_corpus edit was needed because its tests include_str! the reading.rs source, and its assertions are unchanged. The list simply under-specified these files; the split itself is not at fault.

findings.summary: reading_source() in the refusal corpus lists the child files by hand, so a future child module has to be added to the list by hand.
findings.evidence: The function joins seven named include_str! paths. If a check function moves to a new, unlisted file, the source-text tests (split on `pub fn check_...(`, function_body) would most likely fail rather than pass silently. It is still a second place to update. A comment in reading.rs pointing at this list would help.

findings.summary: Several functions changed from private to pub(super) so that sibling modules can call them, which widens visibility a little within reading.
findings.evidence: For example, terms.rs: `pub(super) fn plain_line`, `pub(super) fn without_quoted_spans`, and many `pub(super) const` items in surveys.rs. The criteria allow this, and it is limited to the reading module tree.

summary: The candidate splits crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs into seven child modules under reading/: retry, topics, checks, outcome, terms, surveys and replay. It re-exports them with `pub use <mod>::*`. The parent file's production code now ends at line 1361, where its test module starts. That is under the 1500-line limit it breached. The largest child, surveys.rs, has 996 lines in total. I compared each new file with the base file using `git diff --numstat --diff-algorithm=histogram`. Only about 7 to 47 lines per child file fail to line up with the base. That count matches the lines I found by search: the `//!` header, `use super::*;`, and the `pub(super)`/`pub(crate)` visibility changes. The few extra lines are probably rustfmt re-wrapping lines the longer visibility made too long. Outside reading/, callers are untouched. All 172 unit tests stay in reading.rs, and no `#[test]` line was added or removed anywhere in the diff. I ran the 172 `reading::` tests and the 20 refusal_corpus tests; all passed. The workspace build succeeds, and Athena's recorded CI run shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. Two minor issues: (1) three changed files are not on the expected-deliverables list: reading/replay.rs, reading/surveys.rs and tests/refusal_corpus.rs. The test-file edit was needed because those tests read the reading.rs source text with include_str!, and their assertions are unchanged. (2) The test's list of child files is written out by hand. One limit on my evidence: policy blocked me from filtering the full moved-lines diff, so the pure-move finding rests on the line counts above, the search results, and the unchanged test suite. I did not read every line that failed to line up.
